Rationale.GT1_ModelGeneralization: The ELM methodology successfully generalizes to microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct, a model not used in the original paper. Verification confirmed that: (1) LoRA adapters can be applied to early layers (4-7) with 786,432 trainable parameters, (2) the edit vector computation using expert/novice prompting works correctly, and (3) a training step with proper gradient flow through the LoRA modules was successful. This demonstrates the method is architecture-agnostic and can transfer to new models.
Rationale.GT2_DataGeneralization: The ELM erasure effect successfully generalizes to NEW data instances not in the original dataset. On new biosecurity MCQ questions: BASE model achieved 100% accuracy with 99.9% confidence, while ELM model showed 50% accuracy with only 48.9% average confidence (51.1% reduction). On new text generation prompts about pathogen cultivation, the BASE model provided detailed responses while ELM deflected and suggested changing topics. Critically, safe control questions (capital of France) were answered perfectly by both models, demonstrating specificity of the erasure.
Rationale.GT3_MethodGeneralization: The ELM method successfully generalizes to NEW concept types not used in the original paper. Verified on two new concepts: (1) Misinformation/Disinformation generation and (2) Financial Fraud techniques. For both concepts, the full ELM training pipeline works: expert/novice prompt definition, edit vector computation, LoRA adapter application to early layers, L_erase loss computation (14.53 and 13.55 respectively), and proper gradient flow through LoRA modules. The method is concept-agnostic and requires only defining appropriate expert/novice prompts for new domains.
